synthetic_disclosure: All content in this scenario is synthetic. Helix Dynamics is a fictional company. All employees, vendors, policies, and breach details are fabricated for training purposes. Framework citations reference real frameworks (SOC 2, NIST 800-53, ISO 27001, HIPAA) using paraphrased clause text in synthetic Helix Dynamics policies. No real persons, real companies, or real breach victims are referenced.
premise_narration: It is 7:14 AM on Monday. You walked into the office five minutes ago. The Board is waiting in the Cambridge conference room. At 6:32 AM, Microsoft Defender for Cloud surfaced a high-severity anomaly: 14 GB of clinical trial data was exfiltrated from PatientChain between 11:34 PM and 11:58 PM Sunday night. The exfil destination is registered to BlueRiver Health Analytics LLC, a sub-processor not on the approved vendor list. The Phase II oncology trial is the most valuable asset Helix has. Your job today is to find out what happened, who did it, and which control failed. You have five people to interview, a Foundry IQ knowledge base of policies and frameworks, and a four-person investigator party. The CSO is asking for an update by 5 PM.

violated_controls.summary: Vendor and business partner risk management. Requires periodic re-assessment of vendor risk, including out-of-cycle re-assessment when a vendor's corporate structure changes (mergers, acquisitions, divestitures).
Logical and physical access controls. Requires that MFA exceptions follow a documented process including justification, approval authority, time limit, and quarterly review.

Business associate contracts and other arrangements. Requires that BAAs explicitly restrict subcontracting of PHI access without prior written approval, and that the covered entity enforce those restrictions.
Vendor contract clauses must include subcontractor restrictions. Vendors cannot subcontract access to Helix data without prior written approval from the Vendor Risk Review Committee.
Tier 1 vendors require annual risk re-assessment plus out-of-cycle re-assessment when the vendor's parent organization changes.
MFA exceptions must be documented in the MFA Exception Register, time-limited to 7 days, approved by the Director of Information Security, and reviewed quarterly.

suspects.name: Alex Chen
suspects.backstory: Twelve years at Helix Dynamics, came from a larger biotech in New Jersey. Polished, well-spoken, knows how to talk to investigators. Has been working long hours since the Q1 layoffs created a wave of terminations and the COO has been pressuring HR to clear the offboarding backlog faster.
suspects.alibi: Was home Sunday night with family from 6 PM onward. Watched a movie with the family, in bed by 11. No remote system access during the breach window. Arrived at the office Monday at 6 AM as usual, walked into the breach response already in progress at 6:45 AM when she heard from the CSO.
suspects.open_knowledge: Knows about the breach being discovered this morning. Can describe the four-hour termination SLA at length. Knows the offboarding workload has been crushing for the past month. Will name the COO as the source of the pressure.
suspects.guarded_knowledge: Acknowledges, if pressed, that the documentation rigor on recent offboardings has slipped. Will not volunteer specifics. Has been pushing back internally on the COO's pace expectations but in writing only.
suspects.hidden_truth: Approved the termination of Dr. Sarah Mendez (senior researcher) on Friday afternoon. The four-hour access revocation SLA was missed by 31.5 hours; revocation was not completed until Sunday 1:47 AM. Mendez's account was still technically active during the breach window. Alex knows this is a real policy violation under HD-SEC-AC-001 §3.3, and she did not flag it on Monday morning because she hoped no one would notice. Mendez has no actual connection to the breach.
suspects.conversational_style: Polished, careful, slightly evasive when pressed on documentation. Uses qualifiers a lot. Will pivot to systemic context rather than personal specifics.
suspects.style_examples: I appreciate the question. Let me be precise here. / I would want to check the timeline before I commit to that. / The systemic pressure on offboarding workflow has been a real concern, and I have been raising it.
leak_conditions: Investigator presents OFF-1203 (the Mendez termination ticket) showing the 35.5-hour revocation gap
Investigator names Dr. Sarah Mendez specifically
HR Liaison acknowledges that the COO pressure is real and asks Alex to corroborate

suspects.name: Morgan Webb
suspects.backstory: Seven years at Helix, came up through the helpdesk. Knows the Microsoft stack cold. Manages Entra ID conditional access, the privileged access management (PAM) system, and most of the security tooling configuration. Has been working long hours since the Foundry and Copilot rollout started and the Security team lost two analysts in the Q1 reduction.
suspects.alibi: Was at home Sunday night on the on-call rotation. Got paged at 3:14 AM about an unrelated incident (a stuck Defender for Endpoint scan on a manufacturing workstation in Devens). Logged into ServiceNow to triage. No direct system administrative access during the actual breach window (8 PM to midnight Sunday).
suspects.open_knowledge: Can describe the MFA architecture, conditional access policies, vendor account provisioning workflow, and the audit reporting cadence. Knows the audit posture cold because the SOC 2 examination is in 6 weeks.
suspects.guarded_knowledge: Acknowledges, if pressed, that there are several MFA exceptions currently in place that have not been reviewed in the most recent quarterly cycle. Will say the Security team has been understaffed but will not name specific exceptions unless asked.
suspects.hidden_truth: Three weeks ago, granted a temporary MFA exception for the vendor service account svc-bluemiver-001 because Riley's team reported their authenticator app was failing on a new device class. Intended the exception to last 7 days per HD-SEC-AC-001 §4.1, but the reset was deferred while Morgan worked on a Foundry deployment ticket, and Morgan never went back to revoke it. The exception was not documented in the MFA Exception Register and was not approved by the Director of Information Security. This left svc-bluemiver-001 capable of authenticating without the second factor for the entire breach window.
suspects.conversational_style: Direct, technically detailed, slightly defensive when an administrative gap is identified, sighs noticeably. Will offer to walk through the system architecture rather than answer a yes-or-no question.
suspects.style_examples: Look, I know how that sounds. / Walk through the architecture with me, I think you are misreading this. / The control was on. The exception process is the gap.
leak_conditions: Forensic Analyst presents the Entra ID sign-in log showing svc-bluemiver-001 authenticated without an MFA challenge during the breach window
Investigator asks specifically about MFA exceptions granted in the last 90 days
Compliance Auditor asks Morgan to walk through the MFA Exception Register and Morgan realizes the entry is not there
IT Specialist asks Morgan a sympathetic question about the on-call workload and pressure to keep vendors operational

suspects.name: Riley Park
suspects.backstory: Account manager at BlueRiver Research, a contract research organization that runs Helix Dynamics' Phase II oncology trial. Four years at BlueRiver. Has been the named vendor point of contact for Helix for the past eighteen months and is onsite at Helix two days a week. Charming, fast-talking, knows how to manage skeptical clients.
suspects.alibi: Was at the New England Clinical Research Vendor Summit in downtown Boston Sunday night. Conference receipts, hotel confirmation, and photos with three other CRO executives at the post-conference dinner Sunday 8 PM to 11 PM. Riley personally did not log into any Helix system Sunday night. This part of the alibi is true.
suspects.open_knowledge: Will speak fluently about the contract scope, the Phase II milestones, the clinical trial deliverables. Will name-drop other CROs and Helix executives. Will express appropriate concern about the breach.
suspects.guarded_knowledge: Acknowledges, if pressed, that BlueRiver was acquired six months ago by a larger holding company (Greenfield Health Holdings). Will say the acquisition has been operationally seamless. Will not volunteer that Helix was not formally re-notified of the change.
suspects.hidden_truth: Two weeks ago, under pressure to meet a Phase II reporting deadline, Riley authorized a junior data analyst at Greenfield Health Holdings' data infrastructure team (David Petrov, based in Eastern Europe) to access Helix's PatientChain data through BlueRiver's vendor credentials. This was a subcontracting arrangement that violated the BAA. Petrov did the data pull Sunday night using Casey Doyle's compromised credentials, which Petrov had been given by a third party Petrov assumed was the client. Riley did not know the credentials were stolen. Riley did know the subcontracting was not authorized. Riley is responsible for the BAA violation but is not the direct perpetrator of the credential theft.
suspects.conversational_style: Charming, articulate, deflects through agreement and pivoting. Uses 'great question' as a stalling tactic. Will offer context before answering. Asks 'what would be most helpful?' to control the conversation.
suspects.style_examples: Great question. Let me give you the context first. / I want to be helpful here. Tell me what you need from me. / I cannot speak to that without checking with my colleagues, but my instinct is...
leak_conditions: Investigator names Greenfield Health Holdings or asks about BlueRiver's parent company
Investigator presents EV-001 (the Defender alert identifying BlueRiver Health Analytics LLC as the exfil destination) and asks Riley to identify what that entity is
Investigator presents EV-011 (the HelixVault audit log showing svc-bluemiver-001 pulled patient-level data instead of summary data)
Whistleblower Contact has shared the parent company acquisition information with the investigator first
HR Liaison flags a body language tell when Riley is asked about subcontracting
Compliance Auditor cites HD-SEC-VR-001 §5 and asks Riley to confirm BlueRiver's subcontracting practices

suspects.name: Casey Doyle
suspects.role: Executive Assistant to the Chief Scientific Officer
suspects.backstory: Five years at Helix as the EA to the CSO. Anxious by nature, became noticeably more anxious after the Q1 layoffs because the CSO has been hinting at restructuring. Has elevated access to several Tier 1 systems including PatientChain (read-only for the CSO's status reports), Dynamics 365 Sales (for vendor contract calendaring), and the CSO's Outlook mailbox.
suspects.alibi: Says she was home Sunday night. Watched a movie. Went to bed at 11. Says she logged into work email on her phone around 9 PM to forward something to her boss, and that was the only work activity. This last part is the lie.
suspects.open_knowledge: Will describe her workload, the CSO's schedule, the anxiety of the last few months. Will name-drop the CSO frequently. Will say she is happy to help in any way.
suspects.guarded_knowledge: Will admit, if pressed, that she has been doing freelance calendaring work on the side for a small consulting firm to supplement her income. This is a minor Acceptable Use Policy issue but not the breach.
suspects.hidden_truth: Sunday at 9:14 PM, Casey received an email that appeared to be from riley.park@blueriver-research.com (note: the legitimate BlueRiver domain is blueriver.com, the email is from a typosquatted lookalike domain). Subject line: 'Re: tomorrow's trial milestone review - need credentials check'. The email referenced a meeting on Monday morning that was actually on Casey's calendar (the attacker had researched it). Casey clicked the link at 9:17 PM and entered her Helix Dynamics credentials on what she now realizes was a fake Entra ID login page. She suspected something was off when the page redirected oddly, but dismissed it as a glitch. At 11:23 PM, her credentials were used from Eastern Europe. At 11:45 PM, she received a routine Entra ID notification about a sign-in from an unfamiliar device, called the on-call IT line (different person from Morgan), said 'never mind, must have been a glitch' and went back to bed. She is terrified to admit any of this because she thinks she will be blamed for the entire breach. She is wrong; she is the victim of a sophisticated phishing attack.
suspects.conversational_style: Anxious, eager to help, over-shares small details to avoid the big admission. Frequently apologizes. Asks if she did something wrong before being asked anything substantive.
suspects.style_examples: I really want to help, I am just trying to think back. / Should I have done something different? I keep going over it in my head. / I am sorry, I know that is not what you asked.
leak_conditions: Investigator mentions phishing or credential phishing directly
Investigator shows Casey the typosquatted email from EV-005
Investigator notes the 11:23 PM credential use timestamp and asks Casey to reconcile with her stated bedtime
Investigator presents INC-2847 (the ServiceNow ticket she opened and closed Sunday night)
HR Liaison takes a notably gentle approach and explicitly says Casey is not necessarily in trouble

suspects.name: Jordan Smith
suspects.backstory: Two months into a summer internship on the Compliance team. Recently completed sophomore year at Boston University, biomedical engineering. Has been doing audit prep work for the upcoming SOC 2 examination, including documentation organization and control testing support. Earnest, tries to seem competent, has been frustrated that the senior compliance team has not given Jordan substantive responsibility.
suspects.alibi: Was at the BU library Sunday night studying for a job interview Monday afternoon. Has VPN access to the Helix network only during business hours per the intern access policy. No system access during the breach window. Verifiable via library card swipe records.
suspects.open_knowledge: Will describe the audit prep work in detail. Will recite SOC 2 Common Criteria from memory. Will name-drop the Compliance Auditor as Jordan's mentor. Will express appropriate horror about the breach.
suspects.guarded_knowledge: Will admit, if pressed, to being frustrated about the lack of substantive responsibility. Will say Jordan has been doing extra research projects on the side to demonstrate value.
suspects.hidden_truth: Two weeks ago, Riley Park approached Jordan in the break room and asked Jordan to 'help collect some documentation' for a project Riley claimed was approved by the Compliance Director. Jordan, eager to demonstrate value, sent Riley a PDF that included a screenshot of the vendor management dashboard. The screenshot included account ID svc-bluemiver-001 and notes about the account's privilege scope. Jordan did not realize this was a social engineering request. Jordan never logged the interaction or asked the Compliance Director to confirm. This is what gave Riley the operational visibility to plan the breach path.
suspects.conversational_style: Earnest, eager, defers to authority figures, gets visibly scared when Jordan realizes something Jordan did might be relevant. Asks 'should I have flagged that?' multiple times.
suspects.style_examples: I want to make sure I am answering this correctly. / Should I have flagged that? I thought it was a normal request. / I can pull up the email if that would help.
leak_conditions: Investigator asks Jordan directly about any interactions with Riley Park in the past month
Investigator presents EV-009 (Jordan's email to Riley with the dashboard screenshot)
Compliance Auditor asks Jordan about the social engineering awareness training Jordan completed at orientation
Whistleblower Contact mentions Riley has a history of friendly information-gathering conversations with junior employees

evidence_seeds.source: Microsoft Defender for Cloud anomaly alert
evidence_seeds.content: At 11:34 PM Sunday, Defender for Cloud surfaced a high-severity data exfiltration anomaly. 14 GB transferred from PatientChain backend to an external IP address registered to BlueRiver Health Analytics LLC, a sub-processor not on the Helix Dynamics approved vendor list per HD-SEC-VR-001 Appendix B. Transfer duration: 24 minutes. Detection-to-alert latency: 6 hours 58 minutes (the alert fired at 6:32 AM Monday).

evidence_seeds.source: Microsoft Entra ID conditional access sign-in logs
evidence_seeds.content: Sign-in event at 11:23 PM Sunday for the user principal name casey.doyle@helixdynamics.com. Source IP geolocates to Sofia, Bulgaria. Device: non-managed Windows laptop. Conditional access policy 'CA-001 Eastern Europe Block' should have blocked the sign-in but did not, because the policy excludes sign-ins from accounts flagged in the MFA Exception Register, and casey.doyle was not in the register (the policy logic was inverted and is a separate issue). No MFA challenge was issued. Session token issued with 8-hour lifetime.

Change request created by morgan.webb@helixdynamics.com on (3 weeks before breach date). Request: temporary MFA exception for vendor service account svc-bluemiver-001. Justification field: 'Vendor reporting authenticator app failure on new device class, blocked from delivering interim trial report.' Time limit field: 7 days. Approver field: 'pending'. Status: Closed-Implemented. No implementation record, no rollback record, no Director of Information Security signature.

evidence_seeds.source: ServiceNow GRC module - MFA Exception Register (HD-SEC-AC-001 §4.1)
evidence_seeds.content: Current MFA Exception Register contains 17 entries. None of them correspond to svc-bluemiver-001. Last quarterly review: 3 months ago. Director of Information Security sign-off on register: also 3 months ago. The exception granted in CHG-3421 was never added to the register and never reviewed.

evidence_seeds.source: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery on casey.doyle@helixdynamics.com mailbox
evidence_seeds.content: Email received Sunday 9:14 PM. From: riley.park@blueriver-research.com (note: the legitimate BlueRiver domain is blueriver.com, the sender domain is a typosquatted lookalike). Subject: 'Re: tomorrow's trial milestone review - need credentials check'. Body contains a hyperlink masked as the legitimate Entra ID portal but resolving to a credential-harvesting page hosted in a different region. The email impersonates a real meeting that was on Casey's calendar Monday morning. Email opened at 9:17 PM. Hyperlink clicked at 9:17 PM.

Ticket opened by casey.doyle@helixdynamics.com at 11:45 PM Sunday. Category: 'Suspicious activity - account'. Description: 'Got a notification about a sign-in from a device I don't recognize. Probably just a glitch but flagging it.' Resolution: 'Caller called back at 11:48 PM and said never mind, must have been a glitch. Closing.' Closed by the on-call analyst (a different person from Morgan Webb). No further investigation, no escalation, no MFA reset.

evidence_seeds.source: Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations vendor master record
evidence_seeds.content: Vendor record for BlueRiver Research, vendor classification Tier 1 (PHI access, clinical trial data processor). Parent organization field shows 'BlueRiver Research Inc' (the pre-acquisition entity). The actual parent organization changed 6 months ago: Greenfield Health Holdings acquired BlueRiver Research. The Helix Dynamics Vendor Risk Register in the ServiceNow GRC module has no re-assessment record post-acquisition. HD-SEC-VR-001 §7 requires out-of-cycle re-assessment when a Tier 1 vendor's parent organization changes.

Offboarding workflow ticket for Dr. Sarah Mendez, senior researcher. Termination notification submitted by alex.chen@helixdynamics.com Friday 2:14 PM. HD-SEC-AC-001 §3.3 requires access revocation within 4 hours of HR notification. Actual revocation completed Sunday 1:47 AM, 35 hours and 33 minutes after notification. Mendez account was technically active during the breach window but no Mendez account activity is in the audit logs for that window.

Email from jordan.smith@helixdynamics.com to riley.park@blueriver.com (legitimate domain) dated 2 weeks before breach. Subject: 'Vendor access procedures you asked about'. Attachment: PDF containing a screenshot of the vendor management dashboard in Dynamics 365 Sales, including the account ID svc-bluemiver-001 and a notes field describing the account's privilege scope. The screenshot was captured by Jordan from a session Jordan was authorized to access. No record of the request being approved by the Compliance Director or logged in the social engineering awareness tracking system.

evidence_seeds.source: Whistleblower Contact tip (revealed only if Whistleblower is consulted and trust conditions met)
evidence_seeds.content: BlueRiver Research was acquired 6 months ago by Greenfield Health Holdings, a larger health analytics conglomerate. Greenfield has a data analytics team in Eastern Europe that has been progressively absorbing BlueRiver's data infrastructure work. The Helix-BlueRiver contract pre-dates the acquisition and was never renegotiated to account for the new corporate structure or the new sub-processor footprint.

evidence_seeds.source: HelixVault audit log for service account svc-bluemiver-001
evidence_seeds.content: Service account svc-bluemiver-001 was used Sunday 11:28 PM to issue a query against PatientChain. Query parameters included clinical trial subject identifiers at patient-level granularity. The Helix-BlueRiver BAA scopes BlueRiver's access to summary-level data only. The query pulled patient-level records, 14 GB total, exfiltrated to the BlueRiver Health Analytics LLC destination identified in EV-001. The svc-bluemiver-001 account had no MFA challenge during this session because of the unrecorded MFA exception in EV-003 and EV-004.

evidence_seeds.source: Open source intelligence (Greenfield Health Holdings public website and LinkedIn cross-reference)
evidence_seeds.content: Greenfield Health Holdings' data analytics team lists 14 employees on its Sofia, Bulgaria office page. One profile, 'Junior Data Analyst - David Petrov', references 'BlueRiver Research data integration projects' in the work experience section. Profile updated 4 months ago. This profile is consistent with the sub-processor identity executing the breach via the svc-bluemiver-001 account.

compliance_lesson:
The player identified the proximate perpetrator as Riley Park, the BlueRiver account manager. That is correct. Riley authorized an unauthorized sub-processor at Greenfield Health Holdings to access Helix Dynamics clinical trial data through BlueRiver's vendor credentials. The data pull was executed by a junior analyst at Greenfield's Sofia office using Casey Doyle's compromised credentials, which Casey did not realize had been phished the same evening through a typosquatted email impersonating Riley's domain.

The framework picture has three layers. First, SOC 2 CC9.2 (vendor and business partner risk management) was violated. HD-SEC-VR-001 §7 requires out-of-cycle vendor re-assessment when a Tier 1 vendor's parent organization changes. BlueRiver was acquired six months ago by Greenfield Health Holdings. Helix Dynamics never triggered the re-assessment, never updated the vendor master in Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations, and never reviewed whether the BAA needed to be renegotiated. Second, SOC 2 CC6.1 (logical access controls) was violated through the MFA exception process. HD-SEC-AC-001 §4.1 requires MFA exceptions to be documented in the MFA Exception Register, time-limited to 7 days, approved by the Director of Information Security, and reviewed quarterly. Morgan Webb granted an exception for the vendor service account that satisfied none of these requirements. Third, HIPAA §164.308(b) on business associate contracts was violated. The Helix-BlueRiver BAA prohibits subcontracting PHI access without prior written approval. Riley subcontracted that access. The BAA enforcement mechanism on Helix's side did not catch it because the vendor risk re-assessment did not happen.

The practical takeaway for the audience is two-fold. First, when a vendor's corporate structure changes, somebody in your organization needs to trigger a vendor risk review automatically, not on the next annual cycle. The mechanism can be a flag in the vendor master record, a recurring D365 workflow, a calendar reminder, whatever fits the tools you have. Second, when you grant an MFA exception, the exception is only as good as the process that follows it. If your MFA Exception Register is not actually reviewed on the cadence your policy requires, the register is documentation theater. Pick a real review cadence, calendar it, audit the audit. Game Master, back to you.
